# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

marine_survey <- read_csv(here("data", "theme4_marine_ecology.csv"))
```

# Part A: Faceting Panels

Create a faceted scatterplot showing dolphin detections vs. boat density, with a separate panel for each `site`.

```{r}
ggplot(marine_survey, aes(x = boat_density_index, y = dolphin_detections)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~site) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Site-wise Dolphin Detections vs. Boat Density",
    x = "Boat Density Index",
    y = "Dolphin Detections / Day"
  )
```

# Part B: Exporting Plots with `ggsave()`

Save your styled plot as a high-resolution PNG file at 300 DPI, conforming to standard publication column dimensions.

```{r}
# 1. Build and store the plot object
my_plot <- ggplot(marine_survey, aes(x = boat_density_index, y = dolphin_detections, color = site)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Boat Density Index",
    y = "Dolphin Detections / Day",
    color = "Site"
  )

# 2. Make sure outputs folder is ready
if (!dir.exists(here("outputs"))) {
  dir.create(here("outputs"))
}

# 3. Export to PNG
ggsave(
  filename = here("outputs", "dolphin_detections_plot.png"),
  plot = my_plot,
  width = 150, 
  height = 100, 
  units = "mm", 
  dpi = 300
)
```
